Same zlib upstream version and package set; configuration, deployment steps and documented behavior are unchanged. Set the shipped Zero revalidation interval to 30 seconds and document the revocation window and upgrade behavior. Document database recovery and shutdown timing within the default container and pod grace periods. Document ordered startup, revision-aware Helm readiness, AIO ingress boundaries and cache-only recovery for failed initial synchronization. Document container-readable file secrets, atomic role initialization, missing-role health failures and safe recovery without widening application privileges. Complete operator setup and restore instructions, preserve runtime role restrictions, explain PostgreSQL compatibility and app origin requirements, and pass Zero publication/reset configuration. The Zero and all-in-one images rebuild Litestream v0.3.13 and v0.5.15 with Go 1.27.3 for CVE-2026-111943 and the v5 binary with klauspost/compress 1.18.7 for CVE-2026-63209. native.note: Document desktop cold offline activation from complete unexpired evidence in the OS credential store, exact session binding, fail-closed verification and revocation markers, and native token refresh on socket retry. Existing records need one complete online start; downgrades require signing out stored accounts before installing an older build. Retain queued edits, refuse fallback for trust, HTTP, validation or storage failures, and keep platform runtime qualification explicit. Android cached activation policy is unchanged. Every authenticated native request now persists a refusal fence before I/O, including attachment, notification, cleanup and sync-handshake requests. Binary keyring chunks stay within the Windows blob limit, share credential references, and use a bounded recovery journal. Both earlier protected-record formats require fresh online evidence after upgrade; downgrades require OS credential-manager cleanup. The desktop TLS refusal test fixture now carries a fixed non-secret password because macOS refuses empty-password PKCS#12 imports; test-only, no runtime or documented behavior change.

authentication.note: OAuth registration denials preserve their stable policy code through Better Auth callback redirects. Native browser sign-in retains the grant ID and displays the localized policy message. Document periodic stream revalidation after session revocation; HTTP authorization remains checked against live session state. Invitations remain HTTPS browser links with fragment tokens and backward-compatible acceptance; native task scheme handling is unchanged. Document the current account name, identity update validation, synced display behavior, and managed-account normalization with JSON validation errors. Production startup validates secret length and retained JWKS decryption. The authentication guide links the stopped-replica secret rotation procedure instead of direct replacement. Browser sign-in checks the per-IP ceiling before creating IP-plus-email buckets. The handoff and trusted-proxy guides document that order, unchanged limits and batch-drained cleanup; docs/security.md records the body bound and unchanged TOTP lockout. The authentication guides already changed in this branch document neutral public email sign-up, explicit sign-in without SMTP, admission policy and unchanged native approval. This follow-up preserves that public and native protocol: only identity and password fields reach account creation, and persistence failures use the existing neutral result and timing floor. docs/security.md now describes discarded fields and operator-visible failure logs. No new setup, recovery, native trust, account admission, or credential storage procedure is introduced; managed-account creation retains explicit failures. Unexpected registration-policy failures are logged and return a generic unavailable error instead of a policy refusal carrying the raw message; documented refusals are unchanged.
